descriptionChirho: Distributive adjective/pronoun meaning 'each' or 'every individual one,' picking out members of a group individually rather than collectively. This single sense covers all 82 NT occurrences across all case forms (nominative hekastos, accusative hekaston, dative hekasto, genitive hekastou, feminine hekaste). Used in narrative (Matt 16:27 render to each according to deeds, Matt 18:35, 25:15, 26:22), teaching (Luke 2:3, 6:44, 13:15, 16:5), Johannine discourse (John 6:7, 7:53, 16:32, 19:23), Acts (2:3,6,8,38, 3:26, 4:35, 17:27, 20:31, 21:19,26), and epistolary literature (1 Cor 3:8,13, 7:2,7,17,20,24, 12:7,11,18, Eph 4:7,16,25, 5:33, Col 4:6, Heb 3:13, 6:11, 8:11, 1 Pet 1:17, Rev 2:23, 6:11, 20:13, 21:21, 22:2,12). Cross-linguistic evidence is perfectly uniform: Arb kullu-wahidin (each one), Heb kol-echad/ish (each one/man), Kor gakgak/gak-saram (each/each person), Spa cada-uno (each one), Fra chacun (each), Deu jeder (each), Hin har-ek/pratyeka (each one/each). The auto-clusters for genitive, feminine, and 'one' uses are purely morphological or contextual variants with no semantic differentiation.
